newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico milk farmers want price deregulation.
newsitem.headline: Mexico milk farmers want price deregulation.

text.p: Ranchers from Mexico's northern dairy producing Laguna region said Wednesday their livelihood would be at stake unless milk prices were deregulated in southern and central Mexico.
"Unfortunately it is the small producers who are disappearing," said Laguna Cattle Ranchers' Association leader Felipe Cedillo told Reuters.
Cedillo said there were 600 dairy farmers in the Laguna region who employed 20,000 people directly or indirectly. The Laguna region is in the northern Mexican state of Coahuila.
Milk prices are controlled by the government in Mexico. A liter currently costs 3.60 pesos in Mexico City, and 4.20 in the northern industrial city of Monterrey.
Cedillo noted that Laguna producers have to sell their milk for less in their main market, Mexico City, after transport costs, than in Monterrey, which is far closer.

Mexican milk producers have been pushing for increased prices for several months in newspaper inserts, claiming that low prices are forcing them out of business and have made Mexico the world's biggest milk importer.
There has also been consumer pressure not to raise prices after Mexico's recent economic crisis.
